reference: GNU coreutils base64 under system Bash. A small adapter selects bashbase64 in the candidate and GNU base64 in the reference; GNU is set to -w0 where needed to match bashbase64's documented unwrapped default. The URL-safe case independently maps RFC 4648 URL and standard alphabets with GNU tr.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and documented help metadata
RFC 4648 standard alphabet vectors, including empty input, padding lengths, and bytes requiring +/
Documented unwrapped default and explicit wrapping
Relative file input with an option terminator
Binary-safe decode, ASCII newline whitespace, and ignore-garbage mode
URL-safe encode/decode with an independent alphabet mapping
Invalid-character decode status and emitted prefix behavior
Unpadded final-group bytes and rejection of a single-character tail.
exclusions: Diagnostic wording is not compared; runnable cases require only empty or nonempty stderr.
No large-input, streaming-performance, malformed-padding matrix, or every option spelling coverage.
No deferred operations: bashbase64 performs only bounded fixture I/O and needs no privileged, hardware, network, or external mock environment.

cases.purpose: The compiled loadable is visible to Bash as a builtin, as required for a bash-os loadable.
Bash help exposes the documented synopsis, URL-safe option, and decode tolerance contract.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help bashbase64)
[[ "$help_text" == *"bashbase64 [-d] [-u] [-i] [-w N] [FILE] > output"* ]]
[[ "$help_text" == *"URL-safe alphabet"* ]]
[[ "$help_text" == *"Decode tolerates ASCII whitespace and a leading '0x' tag."* ]]
printf 'help contract ok\n'

cases.purpose: GNU base64 -w0 is the independent standard-alphabet encoder oracle for the RFC 4648 empty, f, fo, foo, foob, fooba, and foobar vectors, plus bytes requiring +/.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashbase64) == builtin ]]; then
  b64() { bashbase64 "$@"; }
else
  b64() { base64 -w 0 "$@"; }
fi
printf 'empty:'
printf '' | b64
printf '\nf:'
printf 'f' | b64
printf '\nfo:'
printf 'fo' | b64
printf '\nfoo:'
printf 'foo' | b64
printf '\nfoob:'
printf 'foob' | b64
printf '\nfooba:'
printf 'fooba' | b64
printf '\nfoobar:'
printf 'foobar' | b64
printf '\n+/ alphabet:'
printf '\xfb\xff' | b64
printf '\n'

cases.purpose: A 58-byte input yields more than 76 encoded characters. GNU -w0 provides the documented bashbase64 default reference, including no line breaks or trailing newline.
An explicit 16-column wrap checks line breaks at a nondefault width and the terminating newline against GNU base64.
Reads a relative fixture whose name begins with a dash after --, comparing file input and option termination with GNU base64.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashbase64) == builtin ]]; then
  b64() { bashbase64 "$@"; }
else
  b64() { base64 -w 0 "$@"; }
fi
printf 'file\000payload\n' > ./-payload
b64 -- ./-payload

cases.purpose: Decodes complete quartets plus a padded final group to binary bytes including NUL and 0xff; GNU base64 is the independent decoder.
Decodes valid base64 split by newline whitespace using the long decode option; both GNU base64 and bashbase64 document and implement this common input form.
With -i, ignores interspersed non-alphabet punctuation while decoding a valid payload, matching GNU base64 --ignore-garbage.
Checks URL-safe encoding and decoding for bytes whose standard encoding uses + and /. GNU base64 plus GNU tr provide an independent RFC 4648 alphabet conversion for the reference side.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashbase64) == builtin ]]; then
  printf '\xfb\xff' | bashbase64 -u
  printf '\n'
  printf '%s' '-_8=' | bashbase64 -d -u
else
  printf '\xfb\xff' | base64 -w 0 | tr '+/' '-_'
  printf '\n'
  printf '%s' '-_8=' | tr -- '-_' '+/' | base64 -d
fi

cases.purpose: Invalid-character decode must fail with a diagnostic. This also compares whether valid decoded prefix bytes are written before the later invalid byte; any difference is retained as a failure.
The documented hand-pasted-input extension accepts one leading 0x tag; the independently known standard vector Zm9v decodes to foo.
Compare decoding of an unpadded final group directly with the available GNU base64, including exact bytes and status.
Missing relative file must fail with a diagnostic.
Explicit dash operand reads redirected stdin.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t bashbase64) == builtin ]]; then
 b64() { bashbase64 "$@"; }
else
 b64() { base64 -w 0 "$@"; }
fi
printf 'f\n' > input
b64 - < input

cases.purpose: Decode ordinary unpadded final groups of two and three alphabet characters, with and without preceding complete groups.
A one-character final group cannot represent a byte; preserve complete preceding output and report an error.
Ignored punctuation does not discard the final decoded byte in an unpadded group.
RFC 4648 URL alphabet values decode an unpadded three-character final group to the documented two bytes.
